_readme: Topic-mapping rules for the Kalshi dashboard. Only the five requested topics are in scope:
gas prices, elections, culture, crypto, golf.
Each rule is evaluated in this fixed order per series: category match, categories[] match,
tag match, ticker prefix match, title substring match. Rules are exact-match only (no fuzzy
matching, no inference) so the same input always produces the same classification, and any
series that matches nothing is excluded and counted rather than guessed into a topic.
Where the category name comes from: GET /trade-api/v2/series returns `category`, `categories`
and `tags` for every series. Values below were observed live from that endpoint on
2026-11-20 (see data/meta.json request log and data/live.json series rows).

crypto.label: Crypto
crypto.why: Kalshi publishes a Crypto series category; settlement source for crypto price series is CF Benchmarks.

elections.label: Elections
elections.why: Kalshi publishes Elections and Politics series categories.

culture.label: Culture
culture.why: Kalshi publishes an Entertainment category and music/film/TV series (e.g. Billboard #1-hit series). Entertainment is broad by nature; every matched series is listed on the site so the mapping can be audited series-by-series.

golf.label: Golf
golf.why: Golf is a tag inside the Sports category, not its own category (observed on /series); matching is therefore tag/prefix based.

gas.label: Gas prices
gas.why: Kalshi's AAA national-average gas-price series (KXAAAGASW) lives inside the Economics category, but Economics also holds ~900 unrelated series, so a category rule would mislabel them. Gas is therefore matched only by ticker prefix / tag / title.

notes.excluded_on_purpose: Sports series other than Golf are excluded even though they carry the largest demo volumes, because the brief limits scope to the five topics.
notes.overlap: A series may map to more than one topic (e.g. a crypto series tagged 'Crypto' inside 'Financials'); all matched topics are recorded on the row.
notes.no_inference: If a series has no category, no tag and no matching prefix, it is dropped and counted in meta.counts.open_markets_belonging_to_untracked_series.
notes.over_broad_avoided: Tags like 'oil' or 'energy' were deliberately NOT used for the gas topic: they also match crude-oil and general energy series, which would mislabel non-gasoline markets as gas prices.
notes.precision_over_recall: Rules prefer precision: a series is only counted in a topic when it matches an explicit category, tag, ticker prefix or title fragment. Series that match nothing are left out and counted in data/meta.json rather than guessed in.
